sdk_candidates.not_asserted: No SDK class, method name, field name or field meaning is claimed for this function, for the +0x4f byte, or for the +0x4c..+0x4f block. The accessor family is an observed layout fact, not an SDK identity.

semantic_contract: Given a receiver R for which R+0x4f is writable, the function stores ((uint8_t)(incoming_stack_word)) at R+0x4f and modifies nothing else. Bits 8 through 31 of the incoming word are discarded at 0x004adc2a, so a caller that passes 0x00000101 stores 0x01, not 0x00 and not 0x101. Because the store is a single MOV byte, every one of the 256 stored values round-trips exactly, including 0x80 and 0xff, which a narrowed or signed reading would get wrong. The function is idempotent for a fixed argument, writes no other receiver byte, makes no call, touches no global, and contains no guard of any kind. A null receiver is not checked and faults. It is the write half of a matched pair with 0x004adc40, which loads the same byte with a byte-wide MOV AL thirty-two bytes earlier in the binary. The receiver is a sub-object rather than the rigblock: the paired getter is called on a rigblock's +0x28 member at 0x00438728 and the +0x44 float getter on cEditor+0x98 at 0x00586f05, and the four bytes at +0x4c, +0x4d, +0x4e and +0x4f each have a matched setter or getter in the 0x004adb60..0x004adc40 range, so they form one four-flag block on that sub-object. The accessors are asymmetric: +0x4c, +0x4d and +0x4f have both a setter and a getter, while +0x4e has a setter only.
classification_rationale: The complete ten-instruction body, the field offset, the one-byte write width, the incoming-word narrowing at 0x004adc2a and the callee-cleaned RET 0x4 were all read directly, and the matched getter 0x004adc40 plus the eight sibling accessors read in the same disassembly window corroborate both the field identity and the flag-block grouping. Seventeen distinct caller functions were confirmed against the recorded xrefs. The behavioural contract -- store the low byte of the incoming word at receiver+0x4f and touch nothing else -- is therefore established, not merely the layout. The material element that stays bounded is the meaning of the byte and of the four-byte block it belongs to: the receiver has two proven provenances (cEditor+0x98 and rigblock+0x28) that do not converge on a named type, no vtable was located, and not one of the seventeen call sites was found to interpret the value, so whether it is a bool, a small enum or a bitfield-style flag cannot be decided. STRONG_SEMANTIC is withheld for that reason and not for the body. STRUCTURAL_ONLY would understate the evidence, since a behavioural claim is made and is fully read from the binary.
semantic_findings: The function is the exact dual of 0x004adc40, which reads the same byte twenty bytes earlier in the binary with a byte-wide load and a bare RET. Together they are the only read/write pair established for the +0x4f flag.

The argument is narrowed at 0x004adc2a with MOV CL,byte ptr [EBP+8] before the store, so the function's parameter type is one byte wide even though the ABI word is four. The reconstruction keeps the uint8_t parameter, which makes the narrowing explicit rather than implicit, and Ghidra's own decompilation already shows `undefined1 param_2`.

The four bytes at +0x4c, +0x4d, +0x4e and +0x4f each have a matched setter/getter pair in the 0x004adb60..0x004adc40 range, so they form one four-flag block rather than four unrelated fields. Only +0x4c, +0x4d and +0x4f have a getter; +0x4e has a setter only.

The float at +0x48 has a setter at 0x004adc00 (MOVSS from the stack) and no getter in the family, which is the mirror image of the +0x4e case. The accessor set is not symmetric, which is a real layout fact and not a gap in the analysis: the window 0x004adb50..0x004adc20 was disassembled exhaustively at 140 instructions with no truncation.

The receiver is the same sub-object as the +0x44 float getter's, and 0x00438700 reaches it as a rigblock's +0x28 member, so the flag block is a property of a sub-object rather than of the rigblock. The SDK's UnkEditorRigblockStruct1 is 0x38 bytes and therefore cannot be this sub-object.

Not one of the seventeen caller functions was found to interpret the stored value, and the paired getter is only ever tested for zero in the sampled uses. A bool, a small enum and a bitfield-style flags byte all fit every observation, so no type is asserted.

clang++ 22.1.8 -m32 -O2 emits `movzbl 0x4(%esp),%eax ; mov %al,0x4f(%ecx) ; ret $0x4` for the reconstruction: 9 bytes against the original's 22, same byte-wide store, same receiver register, same callee-cleaned epilogue.
unresolved_questions: What does the byte at +0x4f mean, and what are the other three flags in the block for? Seventeen call sites were found and none of them was interpreted, so the value's role is unestablished.

What class owns this sub-object? Two proven provenances (cEditor+0x98 through the +0x44 getter's callers, and rigblock+0x28 through 0x00438700) do not converge on a named type, and no vtable was located.
Is the byte a bool, a small enum or a bitfield-style flag? Callers only ever store whole bytes and the paired getter is only ever tested for zero, so the evidence cannot separate these.
Do all seventeen callers pass the same concrete receiver type? Their receiver provenances were not disassembled window-by-window in this batch, so only the fan-in of 17 is independently confirmed.

Why does +0x4e have a setter but no getter in this family, and why does +0x48 have a setter but no float getter? Either they are read by inlined code elsewhere or the getters were never emitted out of line. Not resolved.
Is the redundant spill in all ten family members an artefact of a specific build configuration? It affects no semantics and is not worth further investigation, but it is unexplained.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace exists, so the claim that this flag is written and later read with a meaning is static only.
A runtime pass would need to set the flag through a known call site and observe the paired 0x004adc40 read, to confirm the pairing and to see which values are stored.
The original Cell stage has never been entered in any recorded run, so no stage-level reachability claim is made.
